newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn impressed with Blair's team at Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Bonn impressed with Blair's team at Amsterdam.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government greatly impressed German participants at the European Union summit in Amsterdam but ties with France have not suffered as a result, German delegation sources said on Wednesday.

The sources said Prime Minister Tony Blair's team had got to grips with European policy very quickly since taking office last month. Blair presented himself as a "committed European" during the summit, one German source said.
The Britons had operated with "classic British efficiency", said the source, speaking on condition of anonymity.

When talks got into trouble over a Spanish objection to majority voting plans, Blair and Chancellor Helmut Kohl spoke to Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar outside the conference room to talk him round to a compromise, the source said.

But German delegation members were also keen to emphasise that relations with Paris -- the traditional driving force behind European integration -- had not been damaged by the new warmth between London and Bonn.
New French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin came up to Kohl at the end of the summit to thank him for his cooperation, the sources said.
